newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 20.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The debate on the economy between the leaders of the two major parties - ruling PASOK and conservative opposition New Democracy - was a high-level discussion. After a long time in which observers say PASOK played both government and opposition in Parliament, New Democracy leader Costas Karamanlis's performance yesterday indicated that the party was now coming into its own and ready to be a real opposition.

--Civil servants will have interest rates on housing loans taken out after 1982 rescheduled downwards by up to 3.0 percent. --Both Athens and Nicosia expressed serious reservations about the prospects of success for the expected face-to-face meeting between Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash, due to the continuing intransigence from the Turkish Cypriot and Turkish sides.
--A Greek seaman is being held hostage by Albanian pirates who boarded a Greek speedboat off Sarande yesterday. The pirates are demanding a ransom of ten million drachmas.
--The outcome of yesterday's parliamentary debate - the first in which Simitis faced his new challenger Karamanlis - ended in a tie for both sides, pundits say.

--While Greek and Turkish pop idols Sakis Rouvas and Burak Kut sang about friendship and co-existence on the Cyprus green line, Greek Cypriots fought pitched battles with police to protest the concert. Turkish far-right "Grey Wolf" nationalists also attacked Kut's bus as he travelled to the concert.
--Simitis stole the show yesterday at the parliamentary debate during the second round telling Karamanlis that his speech was full of "damp fireworks".
--Some 12.5 percent of drug users have their first experience during military service, according to a recent report.
--Tears and blood on the Cyprus green line during last night's Rouvas-Kut concert, in which demonstrators held running battles with the police.

--The environment, town planning, and public works ministry will decide today on summer trading and opening hours for public services and retailers. The ministry wants to extend staggered opening hours to the rest of the year to cut down pollution and traffic congestion. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
